# Example check (generated by scripts/check_examples.py)

## ex01: What was the total product revenue in 2018?

verified: True   traps: [3, 4]   tables: ['orders', 'order_items']

```sql
SELECT ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS product_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) = '2018'
```

1 row(s), 0.68s. First 1:

| product_revenue |
|---|
| 7218125.12 |

## ex04: What are the top 10 product categories by product revenue?

verified: True   traps: [3, 4, 6]   tables: ['orders', 'order_items', 'products', 'category_translation']

```sql
SELECT COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name, 'unknown') AS category,
       ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS product_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
LEFT JOIN category_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY product_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
```

## ex05: Which 5 customer states have the most late deliveries?

verified: True   traps: [5]   tables: ['orders', 'customers']

```sql
SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS late_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY late_orders DESC
LIMIT 5
```

| customer_state | late_orders |
|---|---|
| SP | 2387 |
| RJ | 1664 |
| MG | 637 |
| BA | 457 |
| RS | 382 |

## ex12: For each month of 2017, what were the product revenue and the total amount paid?

verified: True   traps: [1, 3, 4]   tables: ['orders', 'order_items', 'order_payments']

```sql
WITH items AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(price) AS item_total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
),
pays AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS pay_total FROM order_payments GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month,
       ROUND(SUM(items.item_total), 2) AS product_revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(pays.pay_total), 2) AS total_paid
FROM orders o
JOIN items ON items.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN pays ON pays.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) = '2017'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
```

| month | product_revenue | total_paid |
|---|---|---|
| 2017-01 | 111798.36 | 127545.67 |
| 2017-02 | 234223.4 | 271298.65 |
| 2017-03 | 359198.85 | 414369.39 |
| 2017-04 | 340669.68 | 390952.18 |
| 2017-05 | 489338.25 | 567066.73 |
| 2017-06 | 421923.37 | 490225.6 |
| 2017-07 | 481604.52 | 566403.93 |
| 2017-08 | 554699.7 | 646000.61 |

## ex15: Which 5 sellers have the highest average review score, among sellers with at least 30 reviewed orders?

verified: True   traps: [8]   tables: ['order_items', 'order_reviews']

```sql
WITH seller_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id, seller_id FROM order_items
),
order_scores AS (
  SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score FROM order_reviews GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT so.seller_id,
       ROUND(AVG(os.score), 2) AS avg_score,
       COUNT(*) AS reviewed_orders
FROM seller_orders so
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = so.order_id
GROUP BY so.seller_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 30
ORDER BY avg_score DESC, reviewed_orders DESC
LIMIT 5
```

| 48efc9d94a9834137efd9ea76b065a38 | 5.0 | 33 |
| 02f5837340d7eb4f653d676c7256523a | 4.83 | 30 |
| d13e50eaa47b4cbe9eb81465865d8cfc | 4.82 | 67 |
| 83e197e95a1bbabc8c75e883ed016c47 | 4.81 | 47 |
| d9bd94811c3338dceb4181f3dbc0c73e | 4.8 | 54 |

## ex16: Which 5 product categories have the lowest average review score, among categories with at least 100 reviewed orders?

verified: True   traps: [6, 8]   tables: ['order_items', 'products', 'order_reviews', 'category_translation']

```sql
WITH order_cat AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id, p.product_category_name AS cat
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
),
order_scores AS (
  SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score FROM order_reviews GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, oc.cat, 'unknown') AS category,
       ROUND(AVG(os.score), 2) AS avg_score,
       COUNT(*) AS reviewed_orders
FROM order_cat oc
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = oc.order_id
LEFT JOIN category_translation t ON t.product_category_name = oc.cat
GROUP BY category
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY avg_score ASC
LIMIT 5
```

| fashion_male_clothing | 3.7 | 111 |
| audio | 3.83 | 347 |
| construction_tools_safety | 3.85 | 166 |
| home_confort | 3.86 | 395 |

## ex26: On which day of the week are most orders placed?

verified: True   traps: []   tables: ['orders']

```sql
SELECT CASE strftime('%w', order_purchase_timestamp)
         WHEN '0' THEN 'Sunday' WHEN '1' THEN 'Monday' WHEN '2' THEN 'Tuesday'
         WHEN '3' THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN '4' THEN 'Thursday' WHEN '5' THEN 'Friday'
```

## ex29: What is the average latitude of sellers in each seller state?

verified: True   traps: [7]   tables: ['sellers', 'geolocation']

```sql
WITH geo AS (
  SELECT geolocation_zip_code_prefix AS zip, AVG(geolocation_lat) AS lat
  FROM geolocation
  GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
)
SELECT s.seller_state, ROUND(AVG(geo.lat), 2) AS avg_latitude
FROM sellers s
JOIN geo ON geo.zip = s.seller_zip_code_prefix
GROUP BY s.seller_state
ORDER BY s.seller_state
```

| BA | -13.25 |

| ES | -20.38 |
| GO | -16.53 |
| MA | -2.5 |
